newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-CASTILLA HAS BIG DAY AS ROCKIES BEAT EXPOS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CASTILLA HAS BIG DAY AS ROCKIES BEAT EXPOS.

text.p: Vinny Castilla never had a better day.
Castilla's fifth hit and second homer of the game, a two-run shot with two outs in the top of the 12th inning, lifted the Colorado Rockies to an 11-9 win over the Montreal Expos Tuesday.

Castilla, who had hit his 26th homer in the second, drilled a 2-0 pitch from Dave Veres (2-3) just inside the left-field foul pole, scoring Neifi Perez. It was Castilla's fourth homer in three days and 13th multi-homer of his career.
"This is great," Castilla said. "Especially with the game-winning homer. I think this was my best day."
"We kept battling back but Castilla had other plans," said Expos manager Felipe Alou.
The win was just the third in 19 July games for the Rockies, who have won six of the eight meetings between the teams this season.
Steve Reed (2-4) allowed just one hit and one walk over three scoreless innings.
Henry Rodriguez, Darrin Fletcher and David Segui homered for Montreal, which has dropped four of its last five games overall.
In Chicago, the Cubs and Braves split a doubleheader.
Greg Maddux pitched his fifth complete game of the season, throwing 63 of his 78 pitches for strikes and helping Atlanta ease past Chicago 4-1 in the first game.
The pitch count was the lowest for a nine-inning complete game since Bob Tewksbury of the Cardinals tossed 76 pitches in 1990.

Maddux (14-3) became the first National Leaguer to win 14 games and is one shy of Toronto's Roger Clemens for the major-league lead. The ex-Cub allowed a run and five hits with no walks and six strikeouts in his seventh straight win and his sixth in as many career decisions against his former team.
Maddux has a 1.43 lifetime ERA against the Cubs, including a 2-0 mark with an 0.37 ERA in three 1997 starts.
In the second game, Chipper Jones's fielding error with two outs in the bottom of the eighth allowed Shawon Dunston to score the go-ahead run as the Cubs won 5-4.

Dunston and Doug Glanville had three hits apiece for the Cubs, who had dropped their first six games against the Braves this season. Andruw Jones's second homer of the game had tied the score in the top of the frame.
In San Francisco, Jeff Kent's second homer of the game -- the 100th of his career -- highlighted a five-run seventh inning as the Giants defeated the Philadelphia Phillies 8-5.
Barry Bonds and J.T. Snow also homered for the Giants.
Mark Gardner (11-4) allowed four runs and seven hits over seven innings. Rod Beck recorded the final out for his major league-leading 31st save.
Mike Lieberthal and Gregg Jefferies hit solo homers for Philadelphia, which has lost three of its last four. Jerry Spradlin (1-6) took the loss.
In Los Angeles, Tripp Cromer's three-run double highlighted a four-run sixth inning as the Dodgers scored an 8-3 victory over the New York Mets.
Tom Candiotti (6-3) got the win, going seven.
Wilton Guerrero had three hits and drove in a run for Los Angeles. Tom Prince, playing in place of an injured Mike Piazza, and Raul Mondesi added homers for the Dodgers.
Edgardo Alfonzo, Carlos Baerga and Butch Huskey homered for New York, whose winning streak stopped at five games
Mark Clark (7-7) surrendered seven runs and 10 hits over 5 1/3 innings.
In St. Louis, Mike Hampton won his fourth straight decision and capped a four-run fifth inning with a two-run single to lead the Houston Astros past the Cardinals, 4-2.
After allowing two runs on three hits in the first inning, Hampton (7-7) gave up just two hits over the final six.
Derek Bell hit a two-run homer for the Astros, who have won a season-high six straight road games.
Andy Benes (6-5) carried a perfect game into the fifth but suffered the loss, allowing four runs and five hits with a walk and eight strikeouts over seven innings.
In Cincinnati, Mike Kelly, Reggie Sanders and Bret Boone all homered in a six-run, seventh-inning rally as the Reds snapped a four-game losing streak with a 7-6 win over the Florida Marlins.
Sanders had two homers in the game
Jeff Conine, Kurt Abbott and Bobby Bonilla homered for Florida, which has dropped four of its last five games.

In San Diego, Greg Vaughn had a pinch homer in the eighth and an infield single that plated the game-winning run in the ninth to lift the Padres to a 3-2 victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates, who lost for the first time in 43 games when leading after eight innings.
